Test Data: One plan with an end date; one without.
Expected Output: With an end date the Total Balance shows the total remaining plan balance and paying it in full ends the plan instantly. Without an end date it shows the patient's net (actual) balance. (Updates the older "Pay Full Amount" naming.)
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1, click Pay Now and choose Total Balance. 2. Assert the amount shown equals Plan1's total remaining plan balance. 3. Pay it in full and assert the plan ends immediately with no further installments due. 4. Open Plan2 for Pat2, click Pay Now and choose Total Balance. 5. Assert the amount shown equals Pat2's net patient balance instead of a plan total. 6. Assert the option is labelled Total Balance in both cases.
Status Comment: Total-Balance Pay Now; end-date vs no-end-date.

Description:
The New 'Status' column is added in the installment section for each installment. It will show the successful, overdue, etc.  status.
Verify that the correct status are displayed in while printing the payment plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = saved plan whose installment list contains at least one successful, one overdue and one outstanding installment.
Test Data: Make a installments with all the available status.
Expected Output: The status column should show the correct status for each installments. The same should be printed while printing the payment plan.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 in detail view. 2. Assert the installment section contains a Status column. 3. Assert the successful installment shows the success status. 4. Assert the overdue installment shows the overdue status. 5. Assert every other row renders its correct status text. 6. Click Print on the plan. 7. Assert the printed installment table includes the Status column with the same statuses as on screen.

Description:
A missed / failed / expired-card / without-gateway installment is marked "Overdue" in the installment table when the plan rolls forward.
- Let a scheduled charge fail (declined card, expired card, or a without-gateway plan where nothing was collected).
- Wait for the plan to move to the next installment.
- Look at the missed installment's Payment column.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = active plan whose next scheduled charge will not succeed (declined card, expired card, or a without-gateway plan that collects nothing).
Test Data: A plan whose scheduled charge did not succeed.
Expected Output: When the system moves to the next installment, the missed one shows an "Overdue" status in the installment table's Payment column. Payment (transaction) tracking shows a Failed status for the credit-card attempt.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and note the next scheduled installment number and date. 2. Let the scheduled charge run and fail or collect nothing. 3. Wait until the plan rolls forward to the following installment. 4. Reopen Plan1 and assert the missed installment's Payment column shows the Overdue status. 5. Assert the following installment becomes the new next-due row. 6. Open Transaction Tracking and assert a Failed status is recorded for the credit-card attempt. 7. Assert the plan's overdue total includes the missed installment amount.
Status Comment: Overdue installment status flow.

Description:
An overdue installment flips to "Paid" once the patient pays it via Pay Now.
- On a plan with an Overdue installment, click Pay Now → Overdue Amount and collect it.
- Re-check the installment table.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = active plan with at least one installment currently in Overdue status; Over1 = the plan's total overdue amount.
Test Data: A plan with an Overdue installment.
Expected Output: The installment's status updates from "Overdue" to "Paid" after the Pay Now collection succeeds.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm at least one installment shows Overdue. 2. Click Pay Now and choose the Overdue Amount option. 3. Submit the payment for Over1 and assert it succeeds. 4. Reopen the installment section. 5. Assert the previously overdue installment now shows the Paid status. 6. Assert the plan's overdue total is reduced to zero. 7. Assert the payment appears in the plan's payments list.
Status Comment: Overdue → Paid via Pay Now.

Description:
Without Gateway → "Yes" on the receipt prompt creates a receipt on the scheduled date with mode "credit card without gateway".
- On the payment plan window, tick the "Without Gateway" checkbox.
- On the prompt "Would you like to create the receipt for payment without gateway?" click YES.
- Check the scheduled date and the resulting receipt.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = a payment plan being created with the Without Gateway checkbox ticked; Date1 = the plan's scheduled installment date.
Test Data: A without-gateway payment plan.
Expected Output: A receipt is created for the scheduled date and the payment mode is recorded as "credit card without gateway". (No real card is charged — see RPP-PLAN-029 for the NO branch, which creates no receipt and no transaction.)
Verification Step: 1. Open a new plan for Pat1 and tick the Without Gateway checkbox. 2. On the prompt asking whether to create the receipt for payment without gateway, click Yes. 3. Save the plan. 4. Let Date1 arrive or inspect the scheduled entry for Date1. 5. Assert a receipt is created bearing the scheduled date Date1. 6. Assert the receipt's payment mode is recorded as credit card without gateway. 7. Assert no real card transaction was sent to the gateway.
Status Comment: Without-gateway YES branch (complements RPP-PLAN-027/029).

Description:
Ticking "Without Gateway" disables the saved-card field so no card can be selected.
- Tick "Without Gateway".
- Try to open/select from the saved-card dropdown.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with at least one saved card available; Plan1 = plan in create/edit mode where a card can normally be chosen.
Test Data: A without-gateway plan.
Expected Output: The saved-card field is disabled/greyed out — a card cannot be selected while Without Gateway is on. (The CC surcharge field is also removed — see RPP-PLAN-011.)
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 in edit mode and confirm the saved-card field is enabled. 2. Tick the Without Gateway checkbox. 3. Assert the saved-card field becomes disabled/greyed out. 4. Attempt to open the saved-card dropdown and assert no card can be selected. 5. Assert the CC surcharge field is also removed while Without Gateway is on. 6. Untick Without Gateway and assert the saved-card field becomes selectable again.
Status Comment:
Without-gateway disables saved-card field."Description: replace ""Without Gateway"" with ""Cash Plan (Without Gateway)"".
Pre-Req/Test Data/Expected Output/Verification Step: use the same terminology wherever ""Without Gateway"" appears.
Functional expectation remains: selecting Cash Plan disables/greys the saved-card/payment-method control."

Description:
Verify the all the available payment methods, existing in the system for Pay now button.
- Verify the generated receipts in the system and It should show in the Payments section of payment plan window.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = saved plan; Method1..MethodN = the non-credit-card payment methods configured in the system such as cash, check or money order.
Test Data: Payment With other methods except Credit card.
Expected Output: The user should be able to make payments with all other existing methods. The receipts created by other methods should be shown in the payments section. Verify the details in each columns for different payment methods.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and click Pay Now. 2. Assert every payment method configured in the system is offered in the method list. 3. Complete a payment using Method1 and assert it succeeds. 4. Assert a receipt is generated for that payment. 5. Assert the receipt appears in the Payments section of the payment plan window. 6. Assert each column of the payment row (date, amount, method, status, reference) is populated correctly for Method1. 7. Repeat steps 3-6 for each remaining method and assert consistent behaviour.

Description:
Detail-view Print for a no-end-date plan prints the same 12 installments shown on screen, with the bottom note.
- Open a plan with no end date (showing 12 installments + the note).
- Use Print (detail view).
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient; Plan1 = saved plan with NO End Date, so the installment section shows twelve preview rows and the bottom note.
Test Data: A no-end-date plan.
Expected Output: The printout reflects the same 12 installments shown on screen and includes the same bottom note explaining why only 12 are shown. (Print contents = Patient Info, Plan Details, Due On, Installments, Payment Method — see RPP-PLAN-040.)
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 in detail view. 2. Confirm the installment section shows twelve rows and a bottom note on screen. 3. Click Print. 4. Assert the printout lists exactly the same twelve installments in the same order and with the same values. 5. Assert the same bottom note explaining why only twelve rows are shown is printed. 6. Assert the printout also contains the Patient Information, Plan Details, Due On and Payment Method blocks.
Status Comment: No-end-date print reflects on-screen 12 installments.

Description:
[New] Pay Now now offers FOUR options - Pay Overdue, Pay Next Installment, Pay Total Balance and Custom Payment - and this final list replaces the earlier three-option list.
- Open a saved plan that has an overdue amount and upcoming installments.
- Click Pay Now and read every option offered in the modal.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved active plan that currently has at least one overdue schedule and at least two upcoming schedules; Card1 = the plan's payment method.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with an overdue amount and pending installments; Pay Now opened from the plan detail view.
Expected Output: The Pay Now modal lists exactly four choices: Pay Overdue, Pay Next Installment, Pay Total Balance and Custom Payment. The older three-option list is no longer shown. Each option can be selected and loads its own amount field.
Verification Step: 1. Open the Recurring Payment Plan window for Pat1 and open the saved Plan1. 2. Click Pay Now. 3. Assert the modal offers the Pay Overdue option. 4. Assert it offers the Pay Next Installment option. 5. Assert it offers the Pay Total Balance option. 6. Assert it offers the Custom Payment option. 7. Assert no additional or obsolete option is present and no option is duplicated. 8. Select each option in turn and assert its own amount field is displayed.

Description:
[New] Pay Now - Pay Overdue collects the total overdue up to today only, and cannot be pushed above that total.
- Open a plan carrying more than one overdue schedule.
- Choose Pay Overdue and check the offered amount against the sum of the overdue schedules.
- Try to type a larger amount.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan holding two or more schedules whose due dates have passed without full payment; Over1 = the sum of those overdue schedule amounts as shown on the plan; Sched1 = the earliest overdue schedule.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with overdue total Over1; Pay Now > Pay Overdue; an amount greater than Over1 typed as the negative attempt.
Expected Output: Pay Overdue offers the total overdue accumulated up to today (Over1) and nothing beyond it - amounts above Over1 are rejected or clamped. Paying Over1 settles all overdue schedules and leaves upcoming schedules untouched.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and note the overdue schedules and the overdue total Over1 displayed on the plan. 2. Click Pay Now and choose Pay Overdue. 3. Assert the amount offered equals Over1 and covers only schedules whose due date is on or before today. 4. Assert no future-dated schedule amount is included in Over1. 5. Type an amount larger than Over1 and assert it is rejected or clamped back to Over1. 6. Submit the payment for Over1 and assert it succeeds. 7. Assert every overdue schedule is now settled and the plan's overdue total reads zero. 8. Assert the upcoming schedules keep their original amounts and due dates.

Description:
[New] Pay Now - Pay Total Balance equals the overdue amount plus every pending installment of the plan.
- Open a plan that has both overdue schedules and pending future schedules.
- Choose Pay Total Balance and compare the amount with overdue + pending.
- Pay it in full and check the plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having Over1 = total overdue amount and Pend1 = the sum of all remaining pending installment amounts, both readable from the installment section.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with overdue total Over1 and pending total Pend1; Pay Now > Pay Total Balance.
Expected Output: The Pay Total Balance amount equals Over1 + Pend1 (the whole remaining plan balance). Paying it in full settles every remaining schedule of the plan and leaves no pending or overdue schedule behind.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and read the overdue total Over1 and the pending installment total Pend1 from the installment section. 2. Click Pay Now and choose Pay Total Balance. 3. Assert the offered amount equals Over1 plus Pend1. 4. Assert the amount is not limited to the overdue portion alone. 5. Submit the payment and assert it succeeds. 6. Reopen the installment section and assert no schedule remains in overdue or pending status. 7. Assert the plan balance shown reads zero. 8. Assert a receipt for the full amount appears in the plan's payments list.

Description:
[New] Pay Now - Custom Payment lets the user type any amount of their choice in a free-entry amount field.
- Open Pay Now and pick Custom Payment.
- Check that the amount field is empty/editable and is not locked to an installment or overdue figure.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved active plan having at least one unsettled schedule; Amt1 = the plan's installment amount; Over1 = the plan's overdue total.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now > Custom Payment; a freely typed amount different from Amt1 and from Over1.
Expected Output: Choosing Custom Payment shows an editable amount field that the user can type into freely - it is not pre-locked to the installment amount or the overdue total. The typed amount is what gets collected when the payment is submitted.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and click Pay Now. 2. Select the Custom Payment option. 3. Assert an amount field is displayed and is editable. 4. Assert the field is not locked to Amt1 and not locked to Over1. 5. Type an amount different from both Amt1 and Over1 and assert the typed value is accepted in the field. 6. Submit the payment and assert the collected amount equals the typed value. 7. Assert the resulting receipt in the payments list shows that same amount.

Description:
[New] Custom Payment smaller than the earliest unsettled schedule pays that schedule partially and the schedule STAYS Overdue because full payment was not received.
- Open a plan whose earliest schedule is overdue.
- Pay a custom amount smaller than that schedule's amount.
- Check the schedule's paid amount and its status.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan whose earliest unsettled schedule Sched1 is already overdue; Amt1 = Sched1's amount; AmtLow1 = any custom amount smaller than Amt1.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now > Custom Payment with amount AmtLow1 (less than Amt1).
Expected Output: AmtLow1 is applied to Sched1 as a part payment. Sched1 shows the reduced outstanding amount but its status remains Overdue, because the full scheduled amount has still not been received. No later schedule is touched.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and note Sched1, its amount Amt1 and its Overdue status. 2. Click Pay Now, choose Custom Payment and enter AmtLow1 (smaller than Amt1). 3. Submit and assert the payment succeeds. 4. Reopen the installment section and assert Sched1 shows AmtLow1 as received against it. 5. Assert Sched1's remaining amount equals Amt1 minus AmtLow1. 6. Assert Sched1's status is still Overdue and not Partial and not Paid. 7. Assert no schedule after Sched1 received any part of the payment. 8. Assert the plan's overdue total is reduced by AmtLow1 only.

Description:
[New] Custom Payment is always applied starting from the beginning of the schedule sequence (earliest unsettled schedule first), never to a later schedule the user might expect.
- Open a plan with several unsettled schedules.
- Pay a custom amount that covers about two schedules.
- Check which schedules absorbed the money and in what order.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having at least three unsettled schedules Sched1, Sched2, Sched3 in date order, each of amount Amt1; AmtTwo1 = a custom amount equal to two times Amt1.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now > Custom Payment with amount AmtTwo1.
Expected Output: The custom amount is consumed strictly from the start of the schedule sequence: Sched1 is settled first, then Sched2. Sched3 and anything later stay untouched. The user cannot direct the money at a schedule out of sequence.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and list the unsettled schedules in date order, noting Sched1, Sched2 and Sched3. 2. Click Pay Now, choose Custom Payment and enter AmtTwo1. 3. Submit and assert the payment succeeds. 4. Assert Sched1 is fully settled. 5. Assert Sched2 is fully settled. 6. Assert Sched3 and every later schedule are untouched with their original amount outstanding. 7. Assert there is no control that lets the user pick a different schedule to apply the money to. 8. Assert the allocation order recorded against the receipt runs earliest schedule first.

Description:
[New] Custom Payment exactly equal to the total overdue clears all overdue schedules and leaves nothing spilling onto upcoming schedules (boundary).
- Open a plan with a known overdue total.
- Pay a custom amount exactly equal to that total.
- Check that no future schedule shows any part payment.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan carrying overdue schedules totalling Over1 and at least one upcoming schedule SchedNext1 that is fully unpaid.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now > Custom Payment with amount exactly Over1.
Expected Output: Every overdue schedule is settled and moves out of Overdue status; the plan's overdue total becomes zero; SchedNext1 receives nothing and keeps its full amount outstanding with its original (not Partial) status.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and note the overdue total Over1 and the upcoming schedule SchedNext1. 2. Click Pay Now, choose Custom Payment and enter exactly Over1. 3. Submit and assert the payment succeeds. 4. Assert every overdue schedule is now settled and none remains in Overdue status. 5. Assert the plan's overdue total reads zero. 6. Assert SchedNext1 shows no amount received and is not marked Partial. 7. Assert the plan's next payment date and amount still point at SchedNext1 unchanged.
Status Comment: not required

Description:
[New] Custom Payment rejects meaningless amounts - blank, zero, negative and non-numeric entries cannot be submitted.
- Open Pay Now > Custom Payment.
- Try to submit with the amount blank, then zero, then a negative value, then letters/symbols.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved active plan having at least one unsettled schedule; AmtValid1 = any small valid positive amount.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now > Custom Payment tried with blank, zero, a negative value, and text/symbol input; then AmtValid1.
Expected Output: None of the invalid entries can be submitted - the Pay button stays blocked or a validation message is shown, and no receipt or transaction is created. A valid positive amount submits normally.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1, click Pay Now and choose Custom Payment. 2. Leave the amount blank and try to submit; assert submission is blocked with a clear message. 3. Enter zero and try to submit; assert it is rejected. 4. Enter a negative value and assert the field rejects it or submission is blocked. 5. Type letters/symbols and assert the field does not accept them. 6. Assert no receipt and no transaction were created by any of these attempts. 7. Enter AmtValid1 and assert the payment now submits successfully.
Status Comment: there is a validation in the amount field that amount should be greater than 0

Description:
[New] A schedule sitting at Partial flips to Overdue once its own scheduled payment day has passed without the rest of the money arriving.
- Start from a future schedule that is marked Partial after a custom payment.
- Let its scheduled date pass with no further payment.
- Re-check its status on the plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan containing SchedP1 = an upcoming schedule already marked Partial from an earlier custom payment, with a remaining unpaid portion and a scheduled date that can be allowed to pass.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with SchedP1 in Partial status; no further payment made before SchedP1's scheduled date passes.
Expected Output: Once SchedP1's scheduled payment day has passed and the balance of that schedule is still unpaid, its status automatically changes from Partial to Overdue, and its unpaid remainder is counted in the plan's overdue total.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm SchedP1 currently shows Partial with a remaining unpaid portion. 2. Note the plan's overdue total before the date passes. 3. Allow SchedP1's scheduled payment day to pass without making any further payment. 4. Reopen Plan1 and assert SchedP1's status now reads Overdue. 5. Assert the amount already received against SchedP1 is still shown and was not lost. 6. Assert only the unpaid remainder of SchedP1 is added to the plan's overdue total. 7. Assert Pay Now > Pay Overdue now includes that remainder in its capped amount.

Description:
[New] A Partial schedule stays Partial as long as its scheduled payment day has not yet arrived (it must not be shown as overdue early).
- Create a Partial future schedule via a custom payment.
- Before its scheduled date arrives, re-open the plan.
- Confirm the status is still Partial and the amount is not counted as overdue.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan containing SchedP1 = an upcoming schedule marked Partial after a custom payment, whose scheduled date is still in the future.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with SchedP1 marked Partial and its scheduled date not yet reached.
Expected Output: SchedP1 continues to show Partial until its scheduled day passes. Its unpaid remainder is not included in the plan's overdue total and Pay Overdue does not offer it.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm SchedP1 is marked Partial with a future scheduled date. 2. Assert the plan's overdue total does not include SchedP1's unpaid remainder. 3. Click Pay Now > Pay Overdue and assert the capped amount excludes SchedP1's remainder. 4. Close the modal, reopen the plan later on the same day and assert SchedP1 still reads Partial. 5. Assert SchedP1 is not styled or reported as overdue anywhere on the screen or in the print view.
Test Case Relevance: Schedule status - Partial before due date

Description:
[New] Installments section status vocabulary - a schedule whose date has passed with no payment received is shown as Outstanding.
- Let a scheduled date pass with no money collected.
- Open the plan's Installments section and read the status column for that row.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having SchedO1 = a schedule whose date has passed and against which no payment at all was received.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with SchedO1 past-dated and completely unpaid.
Expected Output: The Installments section status column shows Outstanding for SchedO1 - the wording used when the date has passed and the payment has not been received.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and go to the Installments section. 2. Locate the row for SchedO1 whose scheduled date is in the past. 3. Assert no payment amount is recorded against SchedO1. 4. Assert the status column for SchedO1 reads Outstanding. 5. Assert the status wording is spelled and cased consistently with the other rows. 6. Print the plan and assert the same Outstanding status appears on the printout.
Status Comment:
"Description: replace ""Outstanding"" with ""Overdue"".
Expected Output: use ""A past-due installment with no payment is shown as Overdue.""
Verification Step: assert the status value is Overdue.
Reason: keep installment status vocabulary consistent with the final Pay Overdue flow and RPP-PLAN-064/065."

Description:
[New] Installments section status vocabulary - a schedule whose payment has been fully received is shown as Success.
- Let a scheduled charge run successfully (or collect it via Pay Now).
- Read the status column for that installment row.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having SchedS1 = a schedule for which the full scheduled amount has been received; Amt1 = that schedule's amount.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with SchedS1 fully collected for Amt1.
Expected Output: The Installments section status column shows Success for SchedS1, the payment amount recorded equals Amt1, and the running balance drops accordingly.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and go to the Installments section. 2. Locate the row for SchedS1. 3. Assert the payment recorded against SchedS1 equals its full amount Amt1. 4. Assert the status column for SchedS1 reads Success. 5. Assert the running balance column decreases by Amt1 on that row. 6. Assert the matching receipt is visible in the plan's payments list. 7. Print the plan and assert the Success status also appears on the printout.

Description:
[New] Installments section status vocabulary - a schedule for which only part of the money has been received is shown as Partial.
- Collect less than the full scheduled amount against one future schedule.
- Read the status column and the amounts for that row.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having SchedP1 = a not-yet-due schedule of amount Amt1 against which only part of Amt1 has been received.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with SchedP1 partially collected via a custom Pay Now payment.
Expected Output: The Installments section status column shows Partial for SchedP1, with the part-received amount and the remaining amount both visible, and the row is not shown as Success or Outstanding.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and go to the Installments section. 2. Locate the row for SchedP1. 3. Assert the payment recorded against SchedP1 is greater than zero but less than Amt1. 4. Assert the status column for SchedP1 reads Partial. 5. Assert the row is not shown as Success and not shown as Outstanding. 6. Assert the running balance reflects only the part payment received. 7. Print the plan and assert the Partial status appears on the printout.

Description:
[New] After a Pay Now payment succeeds the receipt is shown to the user straight away (post-payment receipt view).
- Make a successful payment from the Pay Now modal.
- Check that the receipt view appears without the user having to hunt for it, and that it matches the payment.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved active plan and a working payment method; Amt1 = the amount to be collected through Pay Now.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; Pay Now using any of the four options collecting Amt1.
Expected Output: As soon as the payment is confirmed successful, the system displays the receipt for that payment to the user. The receipt shows the patient, the plan, the amount collected and the payment mode, and it can be closed to return to the plan.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and click Pay Now. 2. Choose a payment option, enter/confirm Amt1 and submit. 3. Assert a success confirmation is given. 4. Assert the receipt view is shown automatically without any further navigation. 5. Assert the receipt shows Pat1's identification, the plan reference, the collected amount and the payment mode used. 6. Assert the receipt carries a payment/receipt number. 7. Close the receipt and assert the user is returned to the plan with the installment section refreshed. 8. Assert the same receipt is also listed in the plan's payments section.

Description:
[New] A cash / Pay Now receipt created from a payment plan cannot be edited (final BA decision - edits are not allowed, only deletion).
- Open a cash receipt created from Pay Now on a payment plan.
- Try to change its amount or any other field.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan; Rec1 = a cash receipt created from Plan1 through Pay Now that has settled at least one schedule.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with cash receipt Rec1; an edit attempt on Rec1's amount.
Expected Output: The cash receipt is read-only - no edit action is offered, or any attempt to change the amount or other details is blocked. A Delete action IS available for the same receipt.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and locate Rec1 in the payments section. 2. Open Rec1. 3. Assert no Edit/Modify action is available for the receipt, or that the fields are read-only. 4. Attempt to change the receipt amount and assert the change cannot be saved. 5. Assert the schedules settled by Rec1 keep their existing statuses after the attempt. 6. Assert a Delete action IS offered for Rec1. 7. Close without changes and assert Rec1's amount is unchanged.

Description:
[New] Deleting a cash receipt that had settled ONE schedule sends that schedule back to Pending when its scheduled date has not yet passed.
- Pay one future schedule in advance with a cash receipt.
- Delete that receipt before the schedule's date arrives.
- Check the schedule's status and the plan balance.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan; Sched1 = a single upcoming schedule whose date has NOT passed; Rec1 = a cash receipt created through Pay Now that fully settled Sched1 in advance.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with advance cash receipt Rec1 settling Sched1; Rec1 deleted before Sched1's date.
Expected Output: Deleting Rec1 reverses the settlement: Sched1 goes back to Pending (because its scheduled date has not passed), its full amount becomes outstanding again, and the plan's paid amount and balance are restored to their pre-receipt values.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm Sched1 is settled by Rec1 and its date has not yet passed. 2. Note the plan's paid amount and remaining balance. 3. Open Rec1 and delete it, confirming any prompt. 4. Assert Rec1 no longer appears in the plan's payments section. 5. Assert Sched1's status is now Pending. 6. Assert Sched1's full amount is outstanding again. 7. Assert the plan's paid amount decreased and the remaining balance increased by the deleted receipt amount. 8. Assert Sched1 is not marked Overdue since its date has not passed.
Test Case Relevance: Cash receipt delete - back to Pending

Description:
[New] Deleting a cash receipt whose settled schedule's date has ALREADY passed sends that schedule to Overdue instead of Pending.
- Pay a schedule with a cash receipt and let its scheduled date pass.
- Delete the receipt.
- Check that the schedule comes back as Overdue and is counted in the overdue total.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan; Sched2 = a schedule settled by cash receipt Rec2 and whose scheduled date has already passed at the time of deletion.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with cash receipt Rec2 settling past-dated Sched2; Rec2 deleted after Sched2's date passed.
Expected Output: After the deletion Sched2 does not return to Pending - because its scheduled date is already in the past it is set to Overdue, its amount re-enters the plan's overdue total, and Pay Overdue offers it again.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm Sched2 is settled by Rec2 and that Sched2's scheduled date is in the past. 2. Note the plan's overdue total before deletion. 3. Delete Rec2 and confirm any prompt. 4. Assert Rec2 no longer appears in the payments section. 5. Assert Sched2's status is now Overdue and not Pending. 6. Assert the plan's overdue total increased by Sched2's amount. 7. Open Pay Now > Pay Overdue and assert Sched2's amount is included in the capped overdue figure.
Test Case Relevance: Cash receipt delete - back to Overdue

Description:
[New] Deleting one cash receipt that had settled SEVERAL schedules reverses every one of them, each to Pending or Overdue depending on its own date.
- Make a large advance cash payment that settles several schedules, some past-dated and some future-dated.
- Delete that single receipt.
- Check each affected schedule separately.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan; Rec3 = one cash receipt whose amount settled several consecutive schedules, of which SchedPast1 has a date already passed and SchedFut1/SchedFut2 have future dates; one of them may be only partly covered.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with cash receipt Rec3 settling SchedPast1, SchedFut1 and SchedFut2; Rec3 deleted.
Expected Output: The single deletion unwinds every allocation made by that receipt: SchedPast1 becomes Overdue (its date has passed) while SchedFut1 and SchedFut2 become Pending, any partial allocation is removed, and the plan's paid amount and balance return to their pre-receipt values.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and list every schedule settled or part-settled by Rec3, noting each one's date and status. 2. Note the plan's paid amount, remaining balance and overdue total. 3. Delete Rec3 and confirm the prompt. 4. Assert SchedPast1's status is Overdue. 5. Assert SchedFut1 and SchedFut2 are both Pending. 6. Assert any schedule that Rec3 had only partly covered shows no residual part payment. 7. Assert the plan's paid amount and remaining balance match the pre-receipt values. 8. Assert no schedule that Rec3 never touched changed status.

Description:
[New] Deleting an EARLIER cash receipt while a LATER receipt also exists only reverses the earlier receipt's own schedules - the later receipt and its schedules stay intact.
- Create a receipt for one schedule, then a second receipt for a following schedule.
- Delete the first (earlier) receipt.
- Check both the reversed schedule and the schedule settled by the later receipt.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan; Rec1 = the earlier cash receipt settling SchedA1; Rec2 = a later cash receipt settling the following schedule SchedB1; both receipts visible in the plan's payments section.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with cash receipts Rec1 (settling SchedA1) and Rec2 (settling SchedB1); Rec1 deleted while Rec2 remains.
Expected Output: Only SchedA1 is reversed - it returns to Pending, or Overdue if its date has passed. Rec2 stays in place and SchedB1 keeps its settled status and amount. No money from Rec2 is re-shuffled onto SchedA1.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm Rec1 settles SchedA1 and Rec2 settles the later SchedB1. 2. Note the status of both schedules and the plan totals. 3. Delete Rec1 and confirm the prompt. 4. Assert SchedA1 returns to Pending, or to Overdue if its scheduled date has already passed. 5. Assert Rec2 still exists in the payments section with its original amount. 6. Assert SchedB1 keeps its settled status and its recorded payment. 7. Assert no part of Rec2 was re-allocated onto SchedA1. 8. Assert the plan's paid amount dropped by exactly Rec1's amount.

Description:
[New] A plan is completed once the TOTAL payment has been received, and the plan status must automatically become Inactive.
- Take a plan with an end date and collect the whole remaining balance.
- Check the plan status right after the last money is received.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan that has an End Date and a known remaining balance Bal1, with every schedule either settled or covered by the final collection.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1; the whole remaining balance Bal1 collected (via Pay Total Balance or the last scheduled runs).
Expected Output: Once the total payment for the plan has been received, the plan is treated as completed and its status flips automatically to Inactive without any manual change. No further deduction is attempted for it.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm its status is Active and its remaining balance is Bal1. 2. Collect the full remaining balance Bal1 so that no schedule remains unpaid. 3. Assert every schedule now shows a settled status. 4. Assert the plan's remaining balance reads zero. 5. Reopen the plan and assert its status has changed to Inactive automatically. 6. Assert the list view shows the plan with the inactive/completed styling. 7. Let the next original schedule date pass and assert no deduction is attempted for the completed plan.

Description:
[New] A plan is also completed when its END DATE has passed, and the plan status must automatically become Inactive at that point.
- Take an active plan whose end date is about to pass.
- Let the end date pass.
- Check the plan status.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan whose End Date can be allowed to pass; the plan may still have unpaid schedules at that point.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with its End Date reached and passed.
Expected Output: Once the end date has passed the plan counts as completed and its status automatically becomes Inactive, with no further scheduled deductions attempted, even if some schedules were left unpaid (those remain visible as overdue/outstanding).
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and note its End Date and current Active status. 2. Allow the End Date to pass. 3. Reopen Plan1 and assert its status has automatically changed to Inactive. 4. Assert no user action was required to change the status. 5. Assert the list view shows the plan with the inactive/completed styling. 6. Assert no new deduction is attempted for the plan after the end date. 7. Assert any schedule left unpaid is still visible with its overdue/outstanding status for follow-up.

Description:
[New] Once ANY payment on the plan has run successfully the user can no longer change the payment method (this is about the payment method only - the term lock is covered separately).
- Compare a plan with no successful payment yet against a plan that has had one.
- Try to change the payment method on each.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved plan that has had at least one successful payment (scheduled run or Pay Now); Plan2 = saved plan of Pat1 with no successful payment yet; Card2 = an alternative payment method available for selection.
Test Data: Plan1 (one successful payment) and Plan2 (no payment yet) of Pat1; an attempt to switch the payment method to Card2 on each.
Expected Output: On Plan1 the payment method section is locked - the card/method cannot be changed once a payment has run successfully. On Plan2 the payment method can still be changed freely. Other editable options on Plan1 behave as per the existing term-lock rules.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm at least one successful payment exists in its payments list. 2. Assert the payment method / card selection is disabled or read-only. 3. Attempt to select Card2 on Plan1 and assert the change cannot be made or cannot be saved. 4. Assert the originally recorded payment method is still shown unchanged after the attempt. 5. Open Plan2, which has no successful payment. 6. Assert its payment method can be changed to Card2 and saved. 7. Make a successful payment on Plan2 and assert its payment method then becomes locked as well.

Description:
[New] Payment deduction keeps running throughout the whole day and is not attempted during night hours - a due installment can be collected at any time of day, not only at one fixed moment.
- Make a plan's installment due and keep it collectable at different times of the day.
- Observe when the deduction attempt happens.
- Confirm no attempt occurs during the configured night window.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = active plan having a schedule due today and a working payment method; Night1 = the configured night window during which deductions must not run; Day1 = the daytime window outside Night1.
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 with a schedule due today; the deduction process observed across Day1 and across Night1.
Expected Output: The deduction for a due installment is attempted at some point during the day window (not only at one fixed clock time) and succeeds when the conditions are met. No deduction attempt is made during the night window Night1 - those attempts are deferred to the next day window.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm a schedule is due today and still unpaid. 2. Observe the plan and Transaction Tracking during the day window Day1. 3. Assert a deduction attempt is made during Day1 rather than only at a single fixed time of day. 4. Assert the successful attempt marks the schedule as settled and creates the corresponding transaction. 5. Set up another due schedule and observe the night window Night1. 6. Assert no deduction attempt or transaction is recorded during Night1. 7. Assert the deferred deduction is attempted again in the following day window. 8. Assert the schedule's due date is not shifted by the night-time deferral.
Test Case Relevance: Deduction run window - day vs night

Description:
[New] The Installments section displays the total payment plan balance and the paid amount, and for a Never ends plan a note is shown at the bottom of the section alongside the 12-installment preview.
- Open a plan with an end date and read the totals shown in the Installments section.
- Then open a plan with Never ends selected and check the totals plus the bottom note.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with Plan1 = saved plan having an End Date, some settled schedules and a remaining balance; Pat2 = patient with Plan2 = saved plan created with Never ends selected (no end date).
Test Data: Plan1 of Pat1 (end date, partly paid) and Plan2 of Pat2 (Never ends) opened in detail view.
Expected Output: The Installments section shows both the total payment plan balance and the paid amount for the plan, and the two figures agree with the schedule rows. For the Never ends plan, twelve preview installments are listed and a note is displayed at the bottom of the installment section explaining the preview.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 in detail view and go to the Installments section. 2. Assert the total payment plan balance is displayed within that section. 3. Assert the paid amount is displayed within the same section. 4. Assert the paid amount equals the sum of the payments recorded against the schedules and the balance equals the unpaid remainder. 5. Collect one more installment and assert both figures update accordingly. 6. Open Plan2 for Pat2, which was created with Never ends. 7. Assert the installment section lists twelve preview installments. 8. Assert a note is displayed at the bottom of the installment section for the Never ends plan, and that the balance and paid amount are still shown.
Test Case Relevance: Installments - totals and Never ends note

Description: [New] The Agreement window is shown only AFTER the payment plan is saved, never while the plan is still being filled in (client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes & Keep it mandatory).
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with no existing payment plan; Set1 = client setting "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes & Keep it mandatory; Plan1 = a new payment plan for Pat1 with all mandatory terms filled (amount, frequency, start date).
Test Data: Pat1, Set1, Plan1 (unsaved new plan with complete terms).
Expected Output: No Agreement window pops up while the plan is being entered or on any field change. The Agreement window opens only once, immediately after the Save of Plan1 succeeds, and it shows the terms that were just saved.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Set1 is configured for the login's client. 2. Open Patient Master > Payment Plan for Pat1 and start a new plan. 3. Fill every term of Plan1 but do NOT save; assert no Agreement window, overlay or prompt appears at any point while typing or tabbing between fields. 4. Click Save. 5. Assert the plan saves successfully and the Agreement window opens on top of the payment plan screen without any extra click. 6. Assert the terms printed in the agreement (amount, frequency, start/end date) match exactly what was saved for Plan1. 7. Close the window and re-save without changing anything; assert the behaviour is consistent with the client setting and no duplicate agreement windows stack up.

Description: [New] When an existing payment plan is updated, the previous agreement is cleared and a fresh agreement carrying the updated terms is shown after the save.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a saved, agreed payment plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan on which the patient already clicked Agree & Continue, so Agreement Doc1 exists at patient level; Term1 = any editable plan term (amount / frequency / end date); Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes but not mandatory.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 with existing agreement Doc1, changed value for Term1.
Expected Output: After saving the changed plan, the old agreement Doc1 is cleared/no longer retrievable and a brand-new agreement window opens showing the updated value of Term1. The Agreement button never serves the stale document again.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and click the Agreement button; note that the existing agreement Doc1 opens and record the terms it shows. 2. Close it, switch the plan to edit mode and change Term1 to a different value. 3. Click Save. 4. Assert a new Agreement window opens automatically after the save. 5. Assert the newly shown agreement reflects the changed value of Term1 and every other current plan term. 6. Close the window, then click the Agreement button again and assert the document offered is the new one, not Doc1. 7. Confirm the old agreement Doc1 is no longer listed/viewable from the plan's Agreement button.

Description: [New] If the newly generated agreement is skipped (window closed), the user can reopen it later from the Agreement button and it shows the NEW terms.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved plan Plan1 that has an earlier agreement; Term1 = an editable plan term; Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes but not mandatory (so skipping is allowed).
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1, changed value of Term1, agreement window closed without agreeing.
Expected Output: Closing/skipping the agreement does not lose it. Clicking the Agreement button on the Payment Plan Info screen reopens the same newly generated agreement with the updated terms, and Agree & Continue is still offered there.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1, change Term1 and Save. 2. When the new Agreement window opens, close/skip it without agreeing. 3. Assert the payment plan screen is usable and the plan record still exists with the updated Term1. 4. Click the Agreement button on the Payment Plan Info screen. 5. Assert the agreement reopens and shows the updated value of Term1, not the pre-change terms. 6. Assert the reopened window still offers the signature capture and the Agree & Continue action. 7. Close and reopen it a second time and assert the same new-terms agreement is served every time.

Description: [New] When the agreement is mandatory and the user skips it on an UPDATED plan, the plan is saved but flipped to inactive.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an ACTIVE saved plan Plan1 that has already been agreed; Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes & Keep it mandatory; Term1 = an editable plan term.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 (active), changed value of Term1, agreement window closed without agreeing.
Expected Output: The plan change is saved, but because the mandatory agreement was skipped the plan status becomes Inactive on the plan window and in the plan list (inactive styling). It does not stay Active.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Set1 = Yes & Keep it mandatory and that Plan1 for Pat1 is currently Active. 2. Edit Plan1, change Term1 and Save. 3. When the new Agreement window opens, close it without clicking Agree & Continue. 4. Assert the updated value of Term1 is persisted on the plan. 5. Assert the plan status now reads Inactive on the plan detail screen. 6. Return to the payment plan list view and assert the row for Plan1 shows the inactive/red styling and an inactive status. 7. Reopen the Agreement from the Agreement button, click Agree & Continue, and assert the plan returns to Active.

Description: [New] When the agreement is "Yes but not mandatory" and the user skips the regenerated agreement, the plan stays active but the old agreement is still gone (cleared on update).
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an ACTIVE agreed plan Plan1 (existing agreement Doc1); Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes but not mandatory; Term1 = an editable plan term.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 with Doc1, changed value of Term1, agreement skipped.
Expected Output: The plan remains Active after the skip, but the stale agreement Doc1 is not served anywhere; only the newly generated (not yet agreed) agreement with the updated terms is available from the Agreement button.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Set1 = Yes but not mandatory and Plan1 for Pat1 is Active with agreement Doc1 already agreed. 2. Edit Plan1, change Term1 and Save. 3. Close the new Agreement window without agreeing. 4. Assert the plan status is still Active on both the plan screen and the list view. 5. Click the Agreement button and assert the document shown carries the updated Term1. 6. Assert the previously agreed Doc1 (with the old terms) cannot be opened from the plan any more. 7. Check the patient-level document area and assert no stale agreement for Plan1 is being offered as the current agreement.

Description: [New] "Agree & Continue" is the activation step - clicking it activates the payment plan and stamps the agreement against the patient.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient without a plan; Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes & Keep it mandatory; Plan1 = a new plan for Pat1 with complete terms.
Test Data: Pat1, Set1, Plan1, Agree & Continue clicked on the agreement window.
Expected Output: On Agree & Continue the agreement window closes, the agreement document is saved at the patient level, and Plan1 becomes Active and starts honouring its schedule.
Verification Step: 1. Create and Save Plan1 for Pat1 so that the Agreement window opens. 2. Click Agree & Continue. 3. Assert the agreement window closes without any error. 4. Assert the plan status on the Payment Plan Info screen is Active. 5. Assert the plan list row for Plan1 shows the active (non-red) styling. 6. Open the Agreement button and assert the agreed document is available with the agreed date/signature captured. 7. Assert the installment schedule of Plan1 is generated and the next installment is highlighted.

Description: [New] Clicking "Agree & Continue" sends the agreement email to the patient when the Agreement event is enabled in the notification preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a valid e-mail address on file; Pref1 = notification preference with event type Payment Plan Agreement enabled for Email; Plan1 = a new saved plan for Pat1; Clinic1 = the clinic e-mail setup used as the sender.
Test Data: Pat1, Pref1 (Agreement event = Email ON), Plan1, Agree & Continue clicked.
Expected Output: One agreement e-mail is queued/sent to Pat1's e-mail address from Clinic1's configured sender address, carrying the agreement of Plan1. The send is logged in the notification/communication history.
Verification Step: 1. Confirm Pref1 has the Payment Plan Agreement event enabled for Email and that Pat1 has an e-mail address. 2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 so the Agreement window opens. 3. Click Agree & Continue. 4. Assert exactly one agreement e-mail entry is created for Pat1 in the notification/communication log. 5. Assert the sender of that e-mail is the clinic e-mail configured in Clinic1, not a system/default address. 6. Assert the e-mail is addressed to Pat1's e-mail on file. 7. Assert the agreement document of Plan1 is attached to the e-mail. 8. Assert no duplicate e-mail is generated if the agreement is only viewed (not re-agreed) afterwards.

Description: [New] No agreement e-mail is sent on "Agree & Continue" when the Agreement event is NOT enabled in the notification preference.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a valid e-mail address; Pref1 = notification preference with the Payment Plan Agreement event turned OFF (or Email channel unticked); Plan1 = a new saved plan for Pat1.
Test Data: Pat1, Pref1 (Agreement event OFF), Plan1, Agree & Continue clicked.
Expected Output: The plan activates normally on Agree & Continue, but no agreement e-mail is generated, queued or logged for Pat1.
Verification Step: 1. Turn the Payment Plan Agreement event OFF in Pref1. 2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 and click Agree & Continue on the Agreement window. 3. Assert the plan activates and the agreement document is still saved at the patient level. 4. Assert no new agreement e-mail row appears in the notification/communication log for Pat1. 5. Assert no error or failed-send entry is produced either. 6. Re-enable the Agreement event in Pref1, re-agree on an updated agreement and assert the e-mail is then produced, proving the switch drives the behaviour.

Description: [New] The agreement is shown as a readable template preview on the patient payment plan setup screen, with the patient's plan terms merged into the template text.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved plan Plan1; Plan1 = plan with amount, frequency, start date, end date and payment method set; Tpl1 = the default Payment Plan Agreement letter template applied to the database.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1, Tpl1.
Expected Output: The agreement opens as a formatted preview of Tpl1 on the patient payment plan setup screen (not a raw file download), showing the patient name and every merged plan term correctly, with no unresolved merge placeholders.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and trigger the agreement (after save, or via the Agreement button). 2. Assert the agreement renders as a readable preview inside/over the payment plan setup screen. 3. Assert the patient's name and demographics merged from Pat1 are correct. 4. Assert the plan terms merged from Plan1 (amount, frequency, start date, end date, payment method) match the plan screen values. 5. Assert no unresolved merge tags or blank placeholder markers remain in the body text. 6. Assert the preview is scrollable and the full template content of Tpl1 is reachable. 7. Assert both the signature capture area and the Agree & Continue action are visible on the preview.

Description: [New] The clinic can capture the patient's signature on the agreement preview and the signed agreement is stored against the patient.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with saved plan Plan1; Sig1 = a hand-drawn signature captured in the agreement signature area; Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes (mandatory or not mandatory).
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1, Sig1 drawn in the signature box, then Agree & Continue.
Expected Output: Sig1 is accepted, rendered on the agreement, and the stored/printed agreement document for Plan1 shows the captured signature along with the signed date.
Verification Step: 1. Open the agreement preview for Plan1 of Pat1. 2. Draw a signature Sig1 in the signature capture area and assert the strokes appear as drawn. 3. Use the clear/redraw control (if present) and assert the area resets, then redraw Sig1. 4. Click Agree & Continue. 5. Reopen the agreement from the Agreement button and assert Sig1 is displayed on the document. 6. Assert a signed date/timestamp is recorded with the agreement. 7. Print or preview the stored agreement document and assert the signature is included in the output.

Description: [New] Verify the "Save and Close" action on the agreement window - the agreement is stored for later without activating through Agree & Continue.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a newly saved plan Plan1; Set1 = "Show Agreement on Payment Plan" = Yes but not mandatory; Sig1 = optional signature drawn on the preview.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1, agreement window, Save and Close clicked (with and without Sig1).
Expected Output: Save and Close closes the agreement window and keeps the generated agreement document available from the Agreement button with any captured content retained; it does NOT act as Agree & Continue, so no agreement e-mail is triggered by it.
Verification Step: 1. Save Plan1 for Pat1 so the Agreement window opens. 2. Click Save and Close without drawing a signature. 3. Assert the window closes with no validation error and the payment plan screen is usable. 4. Click the Agreement button and assert the same generated agreement reopens with its terms intact. 5. Repeat the flow, this time drawing Sig1 before Save and Close, and assert Sig1 is retained when the agreement is reopened. 6. Assert no agreement e-mail was generated by Save and Close alone. 7. Assert the plan status after Save and Close follows the client setting (stays Active for not-mandatory; check the mandatory setting separately). 8. Click Agree & Continue on the reopened agreement and assert only then is the plan marked agreed.
Status Comment:
"Active/Inactive: change to Inactive.
Status Comment: ""Do not automate - provided source only says 'check Save and Close' and does not define the expected state/result.""
Keep it out of automation until the product has a defined expected result."

Description: [New] After the first transaction has run, editing the plan does NOT clear or regenerate the agreement - the agreed document stays locked and intact.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with plan Plan1 that has at least one successful transaction; Doc1 = the agreement already agreed for Plan1; Term1 = any plan field that is still editable after the first charge (e.g. end date or an unlocked field).
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 (one charge run), Doc1, change to Term1 where allowed.
Expected Output: No new agreement window is generated after the first transaction, Doc1 remains viewable and unchanged from the Agreement button, and the agreement content cannot be edited or re-signed.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm at least one transaction has already run. 2. Click the Agreement button and record the content of Doc1. 3. Edit whatever term of Plan1 is still editable (Term1) and Save. 4. Assert no fresh Agreement window pops up after the save. 5. Click the Agreement button again and assert Doc1 is unchanged, including its signature and signed date. 6. Assert the agreement content and signature area are read-only - editing or re-signing is not possible. 7. Assert the plan status is not flipped to Inactive by this save even under the mandatory client setting.

Description: [New] Verify the content of the agreement e-mail - it must carry the agreement document, and the body text (if any) must match the configured template.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with e-mail on file; Pref1 = notification preference with the Payment Plan Agreement event enabled for Email; Plan1 = saved plan for Pat1; Tpl1 = the agreement e-mail letter template, if one is configured.
Test Data: Pat1, Pref1, Plan1, Agree & Continue clicked; inspect the generated e-mail.
Expected Output: The e-mail carries the agreement document of Plan1 as an attachment. Whether the e-mail also carries a text body, and what that body text should say, is not confirmed in the source thread and must be clarified before this row can be finalised.
Verification Step: 1. Enable the Payment Plan Agreement e-mail event in Pref1. 2. Save Plan1 for Pat1 and click Agree & Continue. 3. Open the generated e-mail from the notification/communication log. 4. Assert the agreement document of Plan1 is attached and opens correctly. 5. Assert the subject line is populated and not blank. 6. Record whether a text body is present and capture its exact wording for BA sign-off. 7. Assert the sender is the clinic e-mail setup and the recipient is Pat1's e-mail on file.
Status Comment: Clarification Required - the source thread asks whether the agreement e-mail should carry only the document or also a text body, and the body wording was never confirmed.

Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference selection is visible on the patient payment plan and auto-populates to "No" (do not reconcile) on a new plan.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with no existing payment plan; Fld1 = the Reconciliation Preference field on the payment plan window.
Test Data: Pat1, a brand-new payment plan opened in create mode.
Expected Output: Fld1 is visible on the payment plan window and is pre-filled with the "No" / do-not-reconcile option without the user touching it; the plan can be saved as-is with that default retained.
Verification Step: 1. Open Patient Master > Payment Plan for Pat1 and start a new plan. 2. Assert the Reconciliation Preference field Fld1 is visible on the payment plan window and is clearly labelled. 3. Assert Fld1 is pre-populated with the "No" / do-not-reconcile option before any user interaction. 4. Open the Fld1 dropdown and assert all defined options are listed, with the default one highlighted as selected. 5. Save the plan without changing Fld1. 6. Reopen the saved plan and assert Fld1 still shows the default "No" selection. 7. Assert the field is not mandatory - the save completed without any prompt on Fld1.

Description: [New] The Reconciliation Preference selection can be changed at any time, including on a running plan that has already had transactions, and the change persists.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with an active running plan Plan1 that has at least one successful transaction; Fld1 = the Reconciliation Preference field; Opt1 = the default "No" option; Opt2 = any non-default reconciliation option.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 (already charged once), change Fld1 from Opt1 to Opt2 and back.
Expected Output: Fld1 remains editable after the first transaction (it is not covered by the term lock). Switching between Opt1 and Opt2 saves cleanly, survives a reopen, and does not alter the plan amount, frequency, dates or installment rows.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm at least one transaction has run and the locked terms (amount/frequency/start date) are read-only. 2. Assert Fld1 is still enabled and selectable. 3. Change Fld1 from Opt1 to Opt2 and Save. 4. Reopen Plan1 and assert Fld1 shows Opt2. 5. Assert the installment table, amounts and dates are unchanged by the preference switch. 6. Change Fld1 back to Opt1, Save and reopen; assert Opt1 is retained. 7. Assert no agreement window is triggered and the plan status is unchanged by editing Fld1 alone.

Description: [New] Payment plan screens and setups are available to a client WITHOUT OpenEdge configured - only the Payment Method area is greyed out.
Pre-requisite Data: Cli1 = a client/database where the OpenEdge gateway is NOT configured; Pat1 = a patient in Cli1; Scr1 = Patient Master > Payment Plan window; Scr2 = the Payment Plan Template setup screen; Scr3 = the plan-level tracking screen.
Test Data: Log in to Cli1, open Scr1 for Pat1, Scr2 and Scr3.
Expected Output: All payment plan screens, menus and setups open normally for Cli1. Only the Payment Method / card section on the plan window is greyed out (visible but not usable); nothing else is hidden or blocked.
Verification Step: 1. Log in to Cli1 where OpenEdge is not configured. 2. Open Scr1 for Pat1 and assert the payment plan window loads with all sections (terms, due on, installments, reconciliation preference). 3. Assert the Payment Method / saved-card area is displayed but greyed out and cannot be edited or opened. 4. Assert every other field on Scr1 is fully editable. 5. Open Scr2 and assert the payment plan template setup is reachable and editable. 6. Open Scr3 and assert the plan-level tracking screen loads with its filters. 7. Assert no error or 'feature not enabled' message blocks access to any of these screens.

Description: [New] A client without OpenEdge can create, save and activate a complete payment plan end-to-end even though no card can be attached.
Pre-requisite Data: Cli1 = client without OpenEdge configured; Pat1 = patient in Cli1; Plan1 = a new plan with amount, frequency, start date and end date but no payment method.
Test Data: Cli1, Pat1, Plan1 saved without any card.
Expected Output: Plan1 saves successfully with no card, the installment schedule is generated and displayed, the plan appears in the list and plan-level tracking, and the agreement flow (if enabled) works normally.
Verification Step: 1. In Cli1, create Plan1 for Pat1 filling all terms and leaving the greyed-out Payment Method untouched. 2. Click Save and assert the plan saves with no validation error demanding a card. 3. Assert the installment schedule is generated and matches the entered terms. 4. Assert the plan appears in the patient's payment plan list and in the plan-level tracking screen. 5. If the agreement client setting is enabled, assert the agreement window behaves exactly as for a gateway client. 6. Assert the plan status is Active (or Inactive only if a mandatory agreement was skipped). 7. Assert the Print output of the plan renders without a payment-method section error.

Description: [New] A Without Gateway plan does not create any transaction or receipt automatically when the scheduled installment date arrives.
Pre-requisite Data: Pat1 = patient with a Without Gateway plan Plan1 where the receipt prompt was answered NO; Date1 = the first scheduled installment date of Plan1, already reached/passed.
Test Data: Pat1, Plan1 (Without Gateway, no auto receipt), scheduler run after Date1.
Expected Output: After Date1 passes, no payment transaction, no receipt and no open credit exist for Plan1. The installment for Date1 shows as Overdue in the installment table and the plan rolls forward to the next installment.
Verification Step: 1. Open Plan1 for Pat1 and confirm Without Gateway is ticked and no payment method is attached. 2. Let the schedule run past Date1. 3. Open the installment table and assert the installment for Date1 shows Overdue in the payment/status column. 4. Assert the Payments section of the plan shows no auto-generated receipt for Date1. 5. Open payment transaction tracking for Pat1 and assert no automatic transaction was created for Plan1 on Date1. 6. Assert no open credit or unapplied amount was created for Pat1 by the plan. 7. Description: [New] Modified interdependent disabling check - a cash / Without Gateway plan and a saved-card plan for the same patient do not wrongly disable each other's fields.
